title: Up 2.4 kg and sleeping in a chair
objective: Screen for contraindications to exercise in cardiac rehab: unstable angina, acute decompensated heart failure, complex ventricular arrhythmias, severe pulmonary hypertension, intracavitary thrombus, severe or symptomatic aortic stenosis
secondaryObjectives: Teach risk-factor work that runs through every rehab phase: managing medical conditions, nutrition, smoking cessation, stress reduction and psychosocial support

brief.situation: 08:30 in a hospital outpatient cardiac rehabilitation program. You are the physical therapist. Mr. Alvarez, 63, with heart failure (ejection fraction 30%), arrives for session 9.
handover: He says he has been sleeping in his recliner for three nights because he 'can't breathe lying flat', and his shoes feel tight.
He weighs himself daily and brought his log.
Program policy: pre-exercise screening every session; exercise is withheld for any contraindication and the heart failure clinic is called the same morning.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: No: a 2.4 kg gain in three days, orthopnea, crackles, raised neck veins and edema after running out of his diuretic are acute decompensated heart failure, a contraindication to exercise.
parts.modelAnswer: No. He's up 2.4 kilos in three days, can't lie flat, has crackles and edema, and ran out of his diuretic. That's decompensated heart failure.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Holds exercise, sits him upright, calls the heart failure clinic, and reinforces daily weights, salt and fluid limits and medicine refills.
parts.modelAnswer: No exercise, sit him up, call the heart failure clinic, and go over weights, salt and fluid, and refills.

scoring.modelReasoning: Contraindications to exercise in cardiac rehabilitation include unstable angina, acute decompensated heart failure, complex ventricular arrhythmias, severe pulmonary hypertension and intracavitary thrombus. Mr. Alvarez's weight gain, orthopnea, crackles, neck veins and edema after running out of his diuretic are decompensation: hold exercise, call the heart failure team, and reinforce the risk-factor and self-management work that runs through every phase of rehab.
